intro: Hands-on Security+ labs graded in your browser: Linux log analysis and SSH hardening, firewall segmentation, an identity admin console, and attack, incident-response, control and cryptography drills. Simulated, so some details are simplified.

labs.title: Investigate and stop an SSH brute-force attack
labs.summary: Analyze auth.log with grep and pipes, block the attacker with ufw in the right rule order, and harden SSH.
labs.scenario: A monitoring alert shows a spike of SSH logins on web01. You're student with sudo. Investigate /var/log/auth.log, block the attacking address at the host firewall without locking out SSH for everyone else, and harden the SSH server: no root login and no password authentication (keys only). Restart SSH to apply the change.

tasks.text: Read the auth log (it needs elevated rights)
How many failed password attempts are in the log?
Which address is attacking?
Block 203.0.113.45 with ufw, placed above the SSH allow rule
The firewall is still active and SSH is still allowed for everyone else
Disable root login and password authentication in sshd_config
Also confirm PasswordAuthentication no is set, then restart SSH

questions.prompt: Failed password attempts in the log:

hints: sudo grep "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log | grep -c 203.0.113.45 narrows it down.
ufw uses the first matching rule. sudo ufw insert 1 deny from 203.0.113.45 puts the block above the SSH allow.
sudo sed -i 's/PermitRootLogin yes/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config, then the same for PasswordAuthentication, then sudo systemctl restart ssh.
labs.solution:
sudo grep "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log | wc -l        # 15
sudo grep "Failed password" /var/log/auth.log | grep -c 203.0.113.45
sudo ufw insert 1 deny from 203.0.113.45
sudo ufw status numbered
sudo sed -i 's/PermitRootLogin yes/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sudo sed -i 's/PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sudo systemctl restart ssh

Note: 198.51.100.7 had one failure and then a successful login for jsmith. That's worth a follow-up with the user (possible credential compromise), but it isn't the brute-force source.
labs.review: Log analysis with grep and pipes finds the indicators; a host firewall rule contains the source; disabling root and password logins removes the attack path. Rule order matters in first-match firewalls.

labs.title: Segment a three-tier application
labs.summary: Write least-privilege firewall rules between the internet, a DMZ web tier, an app tier, a database tier and a jump host.
labs.scenario:
Zones and hosts:

  • Web server (DMZ) 172.16.10.10: HTTPS from the internet
  • App server 10.10.20.10: TCP 8443 from the web server only
  • Database 10.10.30.10: TCP 1433 from the app server only
  • Jump host 10.10.99.5: SSH (22) and RDP (3389) to any internal server

Everything else is denied.

activities.title: Inter-zone firewall policy
activities.prompt: Build the ordered rule set. Use single IPs, CIDR, or Any; ports can be lists like 22,3389.

tasks.text: Every test packet gets the expected result

hints: Delete the starting rule: it allows anything to the internal network.
Jump host rule: source 10.10.99.5, destination 10.10.0.0/16, ports 22,3389.
labs.review: Segmentation limits lateral movement: each tier talks only to the next one on the port it needs, and administration goes through a single, monitored jump host.

labs.title: Fix identity and access findings
labs.summary: Use an identity admin console to strengthen password and lockout policy, enforce phishing-resistant MFA, and fix account findings from an access review.
labs.scenario: The quarterly access review found: a terminated employee (kpatel) is still active, an intern (jdoe) has admin rights, and the front desk uses a shared account. Policy needs a minimum password length of at least 14, lockout after at most 5 failed attempts, MFA for everyone, and phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2 security keys) for admins. Save each page.

fields.label: Force periodic password changes
fields.help: Current guidance favors long passwords without forced periodic changes unless compromise is suspected.

tasks.text: Disable the terminated user kpatel
Remove admin rights from the intern jdoe
Disable the shared frontdesk account (issue individual accounts instead)
Keep agarcia as an active admin
Minimum length 14+ and lockout after 5 or fewer attempts
MFA required for everyone; FIDO2 keys for admins

hints: SMS codes can be intercepted through SIM swapping; prefer an authenticator app or security keys.
FIDO2/WebAuthn keys are phishing-resistant because they're bound to the real site.
labs.solution: Users: kpatel Disabled, jdoe User, frontdesk Disabled. Password policy: 14 or 16, lockout 5 (or 3). MFA: required for all, authenticator app for users, FIDO2 for admins.
labs.review: Deprovisioning, least privilege, no shared accounts, strong length-based passwords and phishing-resistant MFA are core identity controls on Security+.
